positive_control.evidence: The SAME call, in the same run and from the same fresh administrator session, succeeded for Clayton Stephens - a Technician WITH a home branch - returning his own session with 6 permissions and one branch. C45159-SWITCH.json.
positive_control._question: Did the SAME method find this kind of thing somewhere else in this run?

tried_through_the_screen.evidence: The staff screen itself was driven: the edit dialog was opened and saved, and the branch field is required there. The branches screen (administration/locations) was walked too - it lists branches only and offers no way to assign or unassign a person. PROBE-STAFF-SAVE.json, C45159-ROUTES.json.
tried_through_the_screen._question: Was it reproduced the way a USER does it -- clicking the real UI?

waited_and_retried.evidence: Three separate runs, each from a fresh session: amy.fernandez (Foreman, no branch) refused, craig.mckee (Technician, no branch) refused, clayton.stephens (Technician, WITH a branch) allowed. queue logs c159g, c159h, c159e.
waited_and_retried._question: At least 2 attempts, and the page confirmed quiet before observing?

checked_for_navigation.evidence: Not an in-page action: the refusal is the server's own answer to the sign-in-as request, 'Access denied', with no page involved. The staff save refusal is likewise the server's: 'workplace_id: Missing required parameter'.
checked_for_navigation._question: Did the action navigate, open a tab, or change the URL?

precondition_read_back.evidence: The state was read back rather than assumed. The branch was cleared through the same call the screen makes and the record was re-read afterwards: the branch was unchanged, so the state was never created. The people who already have no branch were read from the staff list (27 active, 34 inactive of 165). C45159-RESULTS.json, C45159-ROUTES.json.
precondition_read_back._question: Was the state you claim to be testing actually built, and read back?

searched_the_repo.evidence: Searched the branch for prior work on this state and for the refusal text: only the case's own authoring records came back (regression-2026-08-26/*, disposition-2026-09-02.json). No BLOCKED-*.md covers it. Nothing in the playbook or the skills.
searched_the_repo._question: Rule 97: exact error text grepped across the repo, playbook, skills and BLOCKED-*.md?

asked_what_would_make_this_my_fault.evidence: Most likely: my own session. An earlier run did exactly that - it became Clayton and then asked to become someone else, which a Technician may not do, so four refusals looked like a rule about branchless people and were a rule about the session I had put myself in. Ruled out by re-running each attempt from a FRESH administrator session, and by the role control: a Technician with a branch is allowed and a Technician without one is refused, so the difference is the branch, not the role and not my session. Second possibility: the staff list's empty branch column is not the app's view of the person - ruled out for administrators (they are offered every branch regardless) by excluding administrators from the candidates.
asked_what_would_make_this_my_fault._question: Name the most likely way this is YOUR mistake, and say how you ruled it out.
